question: In the Forrest Classification, a Forrest Ia lesion (spurting arterial haemorrhage) carries the highest risk of re-bleeding (approximately 90%) and always requires endoscopic haemostasis.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The Forrest Classification grades peptic ulcer appearances: Ia (spurting, ~90% re-bleed) and Ib (oozing, ~50%) are active bleeding requiring endoscopic treatment. IIa (visible vessel, ~50%), IIb (adherent clot, ~25%), IIc (flat spot, ~10%), and III (clean base, ~5%) are progressively lower risk.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Forrest Ia (active spurting) has a re-bleeding risk of approximately 90% without treatment and mandates immediate endoscopic haemostasis. Forrest Ib (oozing) carries ~50% re-bleeding risk and also requires treatment. Together, Ia and Ib are 'high-risk stigmata' requiring intervention.
